properties.name: A near-match across types, or between two records of a line of reasoning, is a note on a successful write, never a refusal
properties.source: @ajs, 2026-10-17: "do 1, 2 and 6 first" (fix 1), with his choices "Note, never refuse" for cross-type and for within a proof
properties.statement:
When a create or revise finds an existing record whose wording is close, reflow2 handles it as follows:
- WRITES and reports the match beside the result (search_first.near_matches, naming each match and its type) when the match is of a different node type, or when both records belong to a line of reasoning (a statement carrying a statement_kind, or an Inference).
- REFUSES, as today, only for a same-type match outside a line of reasoning, with the same three answers: sharpen, distinct_from, replaces.
- The hand-kept list of exempt cross-type pairs is replaced by this rule, and a class test pins the rule.
Measured case to carry over: proof-trial rung 2 on design bbcd344a71ff1cbd, where about 19 creates were refused. A statement there was refused three times against three different nodes, and distinct_from lists of 15–18 ids were needed. Under this rule, recording the same proof needs no distinct_from at all.
